speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I am here to evaluate this newborn presenting with respiratory distress. To begin our assessment, can you tell me how long the baby has been breathing difficultly and was there any trouble during delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given the prematurity and cesarean delivery, have you noticed any specific signs like grunting, nasal flaring, or chest retractions? Also, did the baby require immediate resuscitation or intubation right after birth?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). The clinical picture of a preterm infant born at 32 weeks with immediate signs of respiratory distress, including tachypnea, retractions, nasal flaring, and cyanosis, is classic for RDS due to surfactant deficiency. This diagnosis is supported by the history of prematurity and cesarean delivery without prolonged labor.
